generated_note: Planning document only. This is a prioritized gap map identifying major Saudi statutory instruments not yet among the corpus's 121 tracks. Each gap received a LIGHT verification pass (web search cross-check of existence, approximate Royal Decree number/date, and rough article count) — NOT a full research/verbatim-transcription pass. Decree numbers/dates/article counts below should be re-verified against an official source (laws.boe.gov.sa, the issuing ministry/authority PDF, or Umm Al-Qura Gazette) before any build/transcription work begins. Generated 2026-07-17 by a research-only pass; no existing track files, run_qa_gate.py, or shared wiring were touched.
methodology: Cross-checked the 121 REQUIRED_TRACK_IDS in scripts/validate_corpus_registry.py against the requested focus areas (consumer protection, health/medical regulation, IP beyond trademark/copyright, finance companies/consumer finance, real estate development, zakat, customs, anti-trust/IP enforcement, family/inheritance beyond personal status, government tenders, municipalities, maritime/shipping, insurance, financial leasing, secured lending, anti-dumping, professional services regulation, press/media, elections/municipal councils). For each candidate, ran targeted Arabic web searches against laws.boe.gov.sa (Council of Ministers Bureau of Experts portal), SAMA Rulebook, ministry sites, and legal-reference sites (nezams.com, qanoonsa.com, WIPO Lex) to confirm the law exists, find its Royal Decree number/date, and get an approximate article count.

notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.topic: Movable/secured lending (الحقوق العينية التبعية / رهن المنقول)
notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.finding: Not a standalone law. Registered real rights (mortgage, pledge/lien over movables and immovables) are chapters within the Civil Transactions Law itself, already covered in the corpus as civil_transactions_law (721 Arabic articles, Royal Decree M/191 dated 29/11/1444H). No separate secured-transactions statute was found to exist independently of it.

notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.topic: Off-plan real estate sale/lease (البيع والتأجير على الخارطة) / real estate developers
notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.finding: Already covered — this is what real_estate_units_law and real_estate_units_implementing_regulation are. No separate 'real estate developers law' gap was found beyond what those tracks already represent.

notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.topic: Consumer finance (التمويل الاستهلاكي) as a standalone law
notable_non_gaps_checked_and_excluded.finding: Not a separate statute. Consumer finance is one of the licensed financing-activity categories (alongside real estate finance, SME finance, finance lease, credit cards, microfinance) regulated under the single Finance Companies Control Law (نظام مراقبة شركات التمويل, M/51, 1433H) — see gap entry below. No distinct 'Consumer Finance Law' Royal Decree was found.

gaps.law_name_en: Zakat Collection Law and its Implementing Regulation
gaps.estimated_decree: Original system dates to Royal Decree No. (17/2/28/3321) of 21 Muharram 1370H (establishing zakat/income-tax collection); current implementing regulation issued via ministerial decisions (No. 2082 of 1438H, No. 2216 of 1440H) under ZATCA (formerly GAZT). Administering authority: Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA).
gaps.estimated_article_count: Base law is short (foundational decree); implementing regulation is the operative document, roughly 20-30 articles — needs confirmation
gaps.priority_rationale: Zakat is the primary fiscal levy on Saudi/GCC-owned entities (as opposed to income tax, which is already covered and applies to non-Saudi-owned entities/shares). Virtually every Saudi company must compute zakat; this is one of the highest-frequency compliance regimes in daily legal/accounting practice, and it is conspicuously absent given income_tax_law is already in the corpus.

gaps.law_name_ar: نظام براءات الاختراع والتصميمات التخطيطية للدارات المتكاملة والأصناف النباتية والنماذج الصناعية
gaps.law_name_en: Law of Patents, Layout Designs of Integrated Circuits, Plant Varieties and Industrial Designs
gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree, approx. 1425H (2004), Council of Ministers Resolution
gaps.estimated_article_count: Approx. 60-70 articles across its several parts (patents, IC layout designs, plant varieties, industrial designs) — needs confirmation
gaps.priority_rationale: The corpus already has trademark_law and copyright_law but no patent law — this is the single biggest hole in the IP family. Administered by SAIP (Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property); heavily used in tech, pharma, and industrial-design practice.

gaps.law_name_ar: نظام (قانون) الجمارك الموحد لدول مجلس التعاون لدول الخليج العربية ولائحته التنفيذية
gaps.law_name_en: GCC Unified Customs Law and its Implementing Regulation
gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/41 dated 3 Dhul-Qi'dah 1423H (2002); in force since 1 January 2003
gaps.estimated_article_count: Approx. 190+ articles across several chapters (tariff principles, prohibitions/restrictions, import/export, exemptions) — needs confirmation
gaps.priority_rationale: Customs law governs all cross-border trade into/out of Saudi Arabia and the GCC customs union; extremely high practical frequency for any import/export, logistics, or trade-remedies practice. Administered by ZATCA.

gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/19 dated 23/4/1429H (2008), replacing the 1404H system
gaps.priority_rationale: This is the currently operative statutory basis for consumer/market protection in Saudi Arabia (product quality, mislabeling, deceptive trade practices) administered by the Ministry of Commerce's Consumer Protection Agency. A separate all-encompassing 'Consumer Protection Law' was drafted and put to public consultation (منصة استطلاع) around 2022 but could not be confirmed as enacted — see the unconfirmed entry below. Until/unless that broader law is confirmed in force, this Anti-Commercial Fraud Law is the real, currently binding consumer-facing statute and is a clear gap.

gaps.law_name_ar: نظام مراقبة شركات التمويل ولائحته التنفيذية
gaps.law_name_en: Finance Companies Control Law and its Implementing Regulation
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs SAMA-licensed finance companies across real estate finance, productive-asset finance, SME finance, finance lease, credit cards, consumer finance, and microfinance — i.e., the umbrella law for the entire non-bank consumer/commercial lending sector, which has grown rapidly (BNPL, fintech lenders, auto/equipment finance). Distinct from real_estate_finance_law and real_estate_mortgage_law already in the corpus.

Mandates health insurance coverage for expatriate workers and dependents; directly intersects with labor law and iqama/residency compliance, both high-frequency HR/immigration practice areas. Distinct from insurance_control_law already covered (which regulates insurers generally, not the health-coverage mandate itself).

gaps.law_name_ar: نظام مزاولة المهن الصحية ولائحته التنفيذية
gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/59 dated 4/11/1426H (2005), repealing the 1409H physicians/dentists law and the 1398H pharmacy law
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs licensing and liability of physicians, dentists, pharmacists, and other health practitioners; central to medical-malpractice and healthcare-regulatory practice, an increasingly active litigation area.

gaps.law_name_en: Finance Lease Law and its Implementing Regulation
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs finance-lease contracts (equipment, vehicles, aircraft, real property) including title transfer mechanics; widely used in asset-finance transactions and closely related to real_estate_finance_law and the Finance Companies Control Law gap above.

gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/33 dated 5/4/1440H (2019), replacing the older maritime commerce system
gaps.estimated_article_count: Sizeable consolidated code (multiple hundreds of articles across vessel registration, carriage of goods, maritime liens, collision, salvage) — needs confirmation
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs shipping, vessel registration, carriage of goods by sea, and maritime liability — relevant given Saudi Arabia's port/logistics expansion (Jeddah, King Abdullah Port, Red Sea projects) but a comparatively narrower practice area than the top-tier gaps above.

gaps.law_name_ar: القانون (النظام) الموحد لمكافحة الإغراق والتدابير التعويضية والوقائية لدول مجلس التعاون لدول الخليج العربية
gaps.law_name_en: GCC Unified Anti-Dumping, Countervailing and Safeguard Measures Law
gaps.estimated_decree: GCC Supreme Council resolution 2003; adopted in Saudi Arabia by Royal Decree No. M/30 dated 17/5/1427H (2006), amended by Royal Decree No. M/7 dated 20/3/1434H (2013)
gaps.priority_rationale: Trade-remedies law administered by the General Authority of Foreign Trade (GAFT); relevant to import-competing industries and increasingly invoked as Saudi Arabia diversifies its industrial base, but a narrower practice area than customs or IP.

gaps.law_name_en: Law of the Accounting and Auditing Profession
gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree, replacing the 1412H Certified Public Accountants Law; exact current decree number/date not confirmed in this pass
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs licensing, discipline, and practice standards for auditors/accountants (via SOCPA); relevant to every audited company and to professional-liability practice, but institutional/regulatory rather than transactional in nature.

gaps.law_name_en: Law of the Control and Anti-Corruption Authority (Nazaha)
gaps.estimated_decree: Established by Royal Order No. 65/A dated 13/4/1432H (2011); the Authority's organizational system/statute governs its investigative and disciplinary powers
gaps.priority_rationale: Distinct from anti_bribery_law already in the corpus (which criminalizes bribery itself) — this is the separate statute establishing Nazaha's investigative jurisdiction, administrative-violation powers, and settlement (تسوية) mechanism over corruption offenses. Relevant to white-collar/regulatory-enforcement practice.

gaps.law_name_en: Law of the General Authority for Awqaf
gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/11 dated 26/2/1437H (2016) — note: an earlier search hit suggested M/25, but M/11 is the better-attested number and should be the one verified before use
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs waqf (Islamic charitable/family endowment) administration, a distinct and growing area adjacent to inheritance/personal-status practice and family wealth planning, but narrower in day-to-day frequency than the top gaps.

gaps.law_name_en: Law of the Saudi Council of Engineers
gaps.priority_rationale: Professional-licensing statute for engineers, parallel to the accountants/health-professions gaps above; relevant to construction/infrastructure practice and professional-liability disputes, but a narrower institutional statute.

gaps.estimated_article_count: Not confirmed — needs verification; covers council formation, member elections, election appeals, membership rules, sessions, dissolution
gaps.priority_rationale: Distinct from regions_law already covered (provincial/regional administration) — this governs municipal council elections and local governance. Practically relevant mainly to administrative/local-governance practice rather than commercial or civil practice.

gaps.law_name_en: Law on Printed Materials and Publication (Press Law)
gaps.priority_rationale: Governs press, publishing, and media licensing under the Ministry of Media; lower day-to-day practice frequency than the other gaps, and the media/press regulatory landscape has evolved substantially since 2000 (newer media-sector rules may have superseded parts of it) — flag for a currency check before building.

gaps.estimated_decree: Not issued as a Royal Decree as of the last data found in this pass — a draft was published by the Ministry of Commerce for public consultation on the 'Istitlaa' platform around March-May 2022; no confirmation was found that it has since been enacted
gaps.priority_rationale: If/when enacted, this would likely be a high-priority track (it was designed to consolidate and modernize consumer-rights protections beyond the existing Anti-Commercial Fraud Law). But because enactment could not be confirmed, building it now risks building a draft/superseded text. Recommend periodically re-checking laws.boe.gov.sa for enactment before starting work; the Anti-Commercial Fraud Law gap above is the safer, confirmed target for now.

gaps.estimated_decree: Royal Decree No. M/17 dated 26/1/1441H (2020), 29 articles — but search results indicate it may have been superseded/merged when the new unified Companies Law was issued by Royal Decree No. M/132 dated 1/12/1443H (2022)
gaps.estimated_article_count: 29 articles (original 1441H version); current status relative to the new Companies Law is unclear
